Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may have a potential role in regulating cytokines in postmenopausal endometrium and potentially contributing to irregular bleeding. Uterine natural killer cells are believed to play a possible mechanism in this process.

To synthesize the information, MHT has been found to be associated with changes in cytokine levels, which could influence menstrual bleeding patterns. Specifically, uterine natural killer cells may participate in regulating these changes and contribute to irregular endometrial bleeding that is often observed in postmenopausal women using MHT.
